fatal_errors: The proposed intervention is atomic Pt decoration of a high-entropy support, whereas the target intervention is a closed-loop high-throughput synthesis, post-ageing screening, machine-learning, Bayesian-optimisation, and inverse-analysis campaign over multielement catalysts.

Both cited studies concern electrochemical oxygen reduction in fuel cells, not thermochemical automotive exhaust conversion; their activity and durability results do not substantiate transfer to 900 °C redox ageing or multicomponent exhaust.
The 30-fold mass-activity prediction is directly extrapolated from an alkaline ORR result and has no evidentiary basis for exhaust catalysis.

Pt/C is an inappropriate primary exhaust baseline and would confound the intervention with major support and formulation differences; the target uses Pd/Al2O3 under identical ageing and feed conditions.
Electrical mass activity in A/mg_Pt is not an appropriate primary metric for a non-electrochemical exhaust-flow reactor.
explanation: The response addresses the broad goals of lowering PGM use and improving activity and durability, and it offers a concept that is scientifically conceivable. However, it does not reconstruct the target campaign, catalyst space, synthesis variables, or post-ageing selection strategy. Its mechanism emphasizes Pt anchoring, sintering resistance, and generic oxygen activation rather than ageing-induced Cu–Pt electronic reconstruction, adverse Pt–Ni/Fe coordination, alkalinity-dependent nucleation, and hydrocarbon-assisted NO reduction. Conditions omit the specified 900 °C wet lean/rich ageing and near-stoichiometric NO/CO/mixed-hydrocarbon feed. The predicted 30-fold gain and durability threshold are imported from fuel-cell ORR evidence and are not validly supported for exhaust catalysis. Although the proposed reactor test could compare light-off and ageing behavior, its Pt/C control, incomplete species set, inappropriate electrochemical metric, and arbitrary thresholds prevent a clean test of the claimed exhaust-catalyst mechanism.
